title: Tawbah – repentance
intro: Turning back to Allah after a sin – the way Adam (AS) and Hawwa did.

learn.html: Tawbah is repenting for a sin. It is part of a believer’s everyday life. Tawbah has been known since the time when the first man, Adam (AS), and his wife Hawwa lived in Jannah and made the first mistake. After it, they were the first to repent to Allah and make tawbah.
A person who sins must repent by making tawbah. In Islam, tawbah is made to Allah alone, and straight after the sin.

learn.text: For tawbah to be accepted, the person

items: does not go back to it

learn.title: If someone was wronged
learn.html: If the sin was against another person, the sinner should first apologise and ask them to forgive. If something of theirs was damaged, it must be made good.

learn.label: Words of tawbah
learn.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ مِنْ كُلِّ ذَنْبٍ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
learn.tr: Astaghfirullaaha min kulli dhanbin wa atoobu ilayh.
learn.en: I ask Allah’s forgiveness for every sin, and I turn to Him in repentance.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, so that you may succeed. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nur 24:31)</small>

learn.title: A poem of repentance
learn.html: The Bosnian poet Musa Ćazim Ćatić wrote a famous poem, Tawbah-i nasuh (sincere repentance), in which he falls into sajdah, admits his sins, and asks Allah to heal his soul, strengthen his will and light his way with mercy. Read it with your muallim.

practice.title: Making tawbah
items: Apologise and make good if someone was wronged

questions.q: Is it enough to repent to Allah if we damaged someone’s things?
options: No – we must also apologise and make it good

practice.title: Talk with your muallim
prompts: 💬 Tawbah in everyday life: being ready to admit a mistake to ourselves and others, to be honest, to learn to put things right and to apologise.
